MIT."},{"id":"p2s1","text":"**English** | 简体中文"},{"id":"p3s1","text":"# clawtouch-mcp"},{"id":"p4s1","text":"> **Give your AI agent real hands.**
> An MCP server that turns any MCP-compatible client — Claude D"},{"id":"p4s2","text":"esktop,
> Cline, Continue,
> Cursor, OpenClaw,
> Hermes Agent and any other —
> into something that "},{"id":"p4s3","text":"can move a real mouse and press real keys through a USB HID device."},{"id":"p5s1","text":"## What is this?"},{"id":"p6s1","text":"A standalone Python process that speaks **Model Context Protocol** (MCP) over
stdio and exposes mous"},{"id":"p6s2","text":"e / keyboard primitives — `hid.click`, `hid.type`,
`hid.scroll`, key combos, `hid.screenshot` — to w"},{"id":"p6s3","text":"hatever AI agent you already
use. Under the hood it talks over USB serial to a **ClawTouch HID devic"},{"id":"p6s4","text":"e** (a
Raspberry Pi Pico 2 running the open ClawTouch HID firmware, or any
turnkey ClawTouch box) an"},{"id":"p6s5","text":"d translates each tool call into a real USB HID report.
The target OS sees a **genuine physical keyb"},{"id":"p6s6","text":"oard and mouse** — input arrives on
the same driver path as any plugged-in peripheral, not as a soft"},{"id":"p6s7","text":"ware-injected
synthetic event."},{"id":"p7s1","text":"> 📦 MIT-licensed. No ClawTouch backend, no LLM, no agent loop on top —
> just the raw HID plumbing s"},{"id":"p7s2","text":"o other agent stacks can talk to real hardware."},{"id":"p8s1","text":"> ⚠️ This gives an agent **real keyboard / mouse reach** over a machine —
> the same reach as a pers"},{"id":"p8s2","text":"on at the keyboard. Read Safety first."},{"id":"p9s1","text":"## Why hardware HID?"},{"id":"p10s1","text":"Software automation (PyAutoGUI, OS-level input APIs, multimodal click-the-screen
models) injects **s"},{"id":"p10s2","text":"ynthetic** input events into a session — which requires an
agent process running on the target machi"},{"id":"p10s3","text":"ne, in that user session, with focus.
A USB HID peripheral works the other way around: it emits **re"},{"id":"p10s4","text":"al** HID reports
that travel the standard OS HID driver stack, exactly like a plugged-in keyboard
or"},{"id":"p10s5","text":" mouse. The OS recognizes the Pico natively as a standard USB HID class device
and needs **no mouse "},{"id":"p10s6","text":"/ keyboard driver and no HID agent process** on the input
side of the target. That difference is the"},{"id":"p10s7","text":" whole point of this project — every
other section below just builds on it."},{"id":"p11s1","text":"**The board acts on the machine it is plugged into.** It takes its commands
over the same USB cable "},{"id":"p11s2","text":"it types through, so `clawtouch-mcp` runs on that
machine too — the input side still needs no driver"},{"id":"p11s3","text":". The agent itself can run
elsewhere; see Deployment modes."},{"id":"p12s1","text":"**Good for:**"},{"id":"p13s1","text":"- **Kiosks / locked-down machines** — no input driver or input agent to
install or keep running: the"},{"id":"p13s2","text":" board is a standard USB keyboard and mouse
(`clawtouch-mcp` itself runs on the machine).
- **Access"},{"id":"p13s3","text":"ibility** — let a user drive their own computer via an agent issuing
HID commands, without fighting "},{"id":"p13s4","text":"per-app synthetic-input compatibility.
- **Compatibility testing** — verify your software handles *e"},{"id":"p13s5","text":"xternal* HID input
correctly, which can differ from injected synthetic events.
- **Test rigs** — an "},{"id":"p13s6","text":"agent on your dev laptop drives a test machine that runs
`clawtouch-mcp` (started over SSH, for exam"},{"id":"p13s7","text":"ple — see Deployment modes)."},{"id":"p14s1","text":"**Not for:**"},{"id":"p15s1","text":"- **Mass account creation / multi-account operations** — a single-host tethered
peripheral is struct"},{"id":"p15s2","text":"urally a poor fit; one device drives exactly one target,
and to drive ten machines you buy ten devic"},{"id":"p15s3","text":"es.
- **Application-specific scripted shortcuts** (selectors, fixed-flow scripts for
a particular si"},{"id":"p15s4","text":"te or app). Those belong in agent / RPA frameworks built on top
of this primitive layer, not in this"},{"id":"p15s5","text":"ose belong in agent / RPA frameworks built on top
of this primitive layer, not in this layer itself."},{"id":"p16s1","text":"For standard desktop apps (browser, IDE, office suites) the software-only path
[该节后续省略]"},{"id":"p17s1","text":"## Quickstart"},{"id":"p18s1","text":"> ⚠️ Before you start: read Safety — a connected agent can operate this machine like a person at the"},{"id":"p18s2","text":"e you start: read Safety — a connected agent can operate this machine like a person at the keyboard."},{"id":"p19s1","text":"### What an agent connected to this can do"},{"id":"p20s1","text":"`clawtouch-mcp` turns your agent's tool calls into **real USB HID input** — the
